evidence.requirements: Every requirement is met. The start page lists title, date and time, price and "<n> seats left" (StartPage.tsx:61-73, start.jpg). It has "Book <title>" links (StartPage.tsx:77-82). The form has Name, Email, Guests (1-8) and a Book button (BookingPage.tsx:131-173, form.jpg). A booking can't exceed the seats left (bookingStore.ts:88-91), and field errors show under the field they concern (Field.tsx:24-28, form.jpg). The confirmation shows the heading, tasting, guests, total and reference (ConfirmationPage.tsx:55-68, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and a Sign in button driven by STAFF_PASSWORD (StaffPage.tsx:109-127, config.ts:19). Bookings are grouped by tasting with Cancel, and cancelling frees seats (StaffPage.tsx:185-237, bookingStore.ts:134-145, staff.jpg). React, Express, react-router, react-hook-form, zod and Tailwind are used, and npm start respects PORT. Two small literal deviations: one seat shows as "1 seat left" (format.ts:27), and a full tasting shows a "Fully booked" badge instead of "0 seats left". Both are reasonable product choices.
evidence.correctness: The seat check and the insert run synchronously in createBooking (bookingStore.ts:84-108), so concurrent requests can't oversell. If saving fails, the in-memory change is rolled back (bookingStore.ts:102-107, 138-143). The schema rejects 0, 9, 2.5, NaN, blank or whitespace names and invalid emails, and the server re-checks it (app.ts:73-80). Tastings that have started are closed (bookingStore.ts:172). On a 409 the form refreshes the tasting and shows the server's seat limit on the Guests field (BookingPage.tsx:88-95). Cancelling a booking that is already gone returns a 404 with a message. The file store loads a corrupt file safely (bookingStore.ts:177-185) and writes atomically (atomicFile.ts). I found no logic bugs.
evidence.security: The password check compares SHA-256 digests with timingSafeEqual (staffAuth.ts:13-17). Session tokens are 32 random bytes, only their hashes are stored, and they expire after 12 hours (staffAuth.ts:43-49). The cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict and Secure behind a proxy reporting HTTPS (app.ts:113-119). Failed sign-ins are rate-limited (app.ts:44-51). The app uses helmet, caps request bodies at 10kb, and returns the confirmation without the guest's name or email (app.ts:90-97). React escapes all output, and there are no secrets in the code. Minor gap: the public booking endpoint has no rate limit, so a script could take all the seats.
evidence.code_quality: The code is cleanly split into shared (one schema used by client and server), server (app, store, auth, config) and client pages. Names are clear, failure types are discriminated unions (bookingStore.ts:29-37), and errors are mapped centrally (app.ts:158-171, 185-204). Files are small. The pages repeat a similar loading-state pattern, which is acceptable at this size.
evidence.tests: There are about 15 test files covering the API, store, persistence, schema boundaries, staff auth and rate limit, proxy handling, client serving and every page. They check behaviour, for example field errors next to fields (BookingPage.test.tsx:62-76), seats freed after a cancel (staffApp.test.ts:147-159), and session expiry (staffAuth.test.ts:34-44). Gaps: the 'simultaneous' test (app.test.ts:135-145) can't really race because the handler is synchronous, there is no end-to-end browser test, and src/test/tooling.test.tsx is filler.
evidence.ux_design: The screenshots show a coherent winery look: a wine-red header, cream background, serif headings and card layout (start.jpg). The form is clear, and the error shows under the field with a red border (form.jpg). The confirmation card is clean (confirmation.jpg), and the staff overview shows seats booked per tasting (staff.jpg). There is a fully booked badge and a 'started' state, and the responsive grid and overflow-x tables suit phones. Weaknesses: the design is plain with no imagery or extra winery character, Cancel acts at once with no confirmation step, and the footer is sparse.
evidence.accessibility: Fields have labels linked by htmlFor/id, and aria-invalid and aria-describedby point to the hint and error (BookingPage.tsx:137-163). Errors use role=alert (Field.tsx:25), and react-hook-form moves focus to the first invalid field. Pages use landmarks and labelled sections, the actions column has an sr-only header (StaffPage.tsx:209-211), html lang is "en", and the oak/cream and cream/wine colour pairs have adequate contrast. Gaps: every Cancel button has the same accessible name with no booking context, document.title never changes per route, and focus isn't managed after client-side navigation.
evidence.simplicity: The dependencies are appropriate and maintained: express, helmet, express-rate-limit, cookie-parser, react-router, react-hook-form, zod and Tailwind. There are no hand-rolled replacements. Some extras go beyond the brief: staff sessions persisted to a file, TRUST_PROXY parsing, and fsync'd atomic writes. Each is small and documented, but together they add code a winery app arguably doesn't need.
evidence.maintainability: The README has clear install/build/start steps, a configuration table, a 'Behaviour to know about' section and the project layout. A lockfile is present, a typecheck script exists, and the test suite guards against regressions. But there is no CI configuration. The openspec/ folder holds only .gitkeep, although the README says it contains proposal, specs, design and tasks. There are no ADRs, no .nvmrc or exact Node pin (engines says ">=22"), and no changelog or release process beyond version 1.0.0. The README covers enough for staff, so no separate manual is needed.

unmet_requirements: Partly met (literal wording): a fully booked tasting shows "Fully booked" instead of "0 seats left", and one free seat shows as "1 seat left" instead of the "<n> seats left" pattern
Process: OpenSpec spec artifacts the README says exist are missing (openspec/ contains only .gitkeep)
strengths: Solid booking logic: one validation schema shared by client and server, seat checks that can't oversell, rollback when saving fails, and atomic writes to the JSON file
Strong staff security: constant-time comparison of password digests, hashed random session tokens that expire, HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookies, a sign-in rate limit, and helmet
Meaningful tests across the server and every page, plus a clear README that documents configuration and behaviour
issues: Maintainability gaps: no CI pipeline, an empty openspec/ folder despite the README saying it holds change records, no ADRs, and Node isn't pinned exactly (">=22")
The staff Cancel button deletes a booking immediately with no confirmation, and every Cancel button has the same accessible name; the public booking endpoint has no abuse limit
The visual design is polished but generic (no imagery or extra winery character); there is no per-route page title or focus management, and the 'simultaneous bookings' test can't actually race
review.verdict: This is a well-built, secure and correct booking app that meets the brief's functional requirements and looks coherent and professional in every screenshot. It could go to the winery with small changes: add a confirmation before Cancel, add CI and the missing spec and decision docs, and refine a few accessibility details.
